I need to identify which persistent entity types in the data layer are referenced by the most packages outside that layer. I will rank the top two by approximate package count.

I am exploring the store package to identify persistent entity types and count external references.
I'll identify store-layer entity types and count how many outside packages reference each.

The persistent entity types are Attachment, IdentityProvider, Inbox, InstanceSetting, Memo, MemoRelation, MemoShare, Reaction, and User.

I am expanding the entity list to include UserIdentity, UserSetting, and possibly storepb types. The goal is to count Go packages outside the store layer that reference each type. I will exclude store/, store/db/, store/test/, and store/migration/ from the tally. I am also checking whether proto/gen/store belongs to the data layer.

I will write a Perl script to count unique external packages referencing each entity via `store.TypeName`. I must avoid false matches like `MemoRelation` when counting `Memo`. I will also count pointer types such as `*store.User`.

I will also count references through conversion functions. A Go package is a directory of .go files. The data layer includes store/, store/db/, store/test/, and store/migration/. External packages are server/, cmd/, internal/, and proto/.

message.text:
User is referenced by 7 packages outside the data layer. Memo is referenced by 6. IdentityProvider, InstanceSetting, and UserSetting each show zero references, likely because they are used as storepb types rather than store.IdentityProvider. The entity is store.User.

Still weighing whether to count test packages, proto-generated store types, and whether to split out test directories as separate packages.

Checking whether test directories are separate Go packages. Also verifying whether proto-generated store entity messages qualify as persistent entities, and ruling out enums and helper methods.

Word boundaries prevent false positives between Memo and MemoRelation. Comments may inflate counts slightly. Still deciding whether cmd/memos counts if it only uses Store. internal/idp uses storepb rather than store.IdentityProvider. InstanceSetting may be referenced only through helper methods returning storepb types.

Excluding test packages would still leave User at six and Memo at five, so the top two remain unchanged. Attachment ranks third at three. Proto-generated store types are excluded because the data layer is the store package itself.

Verifying exact package counts by listing the files for User and Memo. Checking whether s3presign imports Attachment directly, since it currently appears to use only Store and ListAttachments.

Confirmed frontend_test.go in server/router/frontend counts User and Memo. rss_test.go is in the rss package. The ranking is solid.

User ranks first with 7 external packages. Memo ranks second with 6. Attachment ranks third with 4. Checking whether frontend_test.go belongs to package frontend or frontend_test.

User is referenced by seven packages outside the data layer. These include server/auth, server/notification, server/router/api/v1, server/router/api/v1/test, server/router/fileserver, and server/router/frontend.

The seventh package referencing User is server/router/rss. Memo is referenced by six packages outside the data layer: server/notification, server/router/api/v1, server/router/api/v1/test, server/router/frontend, server/router/rss, and server/runner/memopayload. The final ranking is User (~7) then Memo (~6).

h11.
1st: `User` (~7 packages); 2nd: `Memo` (~6 packages)

Persistent entities live as `store.*` structs (`store/user.go`, `store/memo.go`, and siblings). Counting `store.Type` uses in Go packages outside `store/` (including `store/db` and `store/test`): `User` appears in `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, and `server/router/rss`. `Memo` appears in those same packages except `server/auth` and `fileserver`, plus `server/runner/memopayload`. Next is `Attachment` at ~4.
